introduced_errors: [Reversed Sequence] `Shipping Label Printed` shown *before* `Package Items` (Expected: Packaging before label)

[Swapped Branch Outcomes] 'No' branch from `Payment Successful?` leads to `Cancel Order` (Correct behaviour), but 'Yes' branch leads to `Shipping Label Printed` which should be *after* material confirmation
[Wrong Causal Direction] `Delivery Confirmed` leads to `Cancel Order` (Expected: Delivery successful after all, so should mark as complete)
[Illogical Loop] `Backorder Items` feeds back into `Order Received`, which will create infinite duplicate orders (Expected: Should feed back to inventory or something to correct stock)
[Skipped Critical Step] Missing steps for inventory check/stock adjustment after order is received and *before* packing.

[Reversed Sequence] Incident is closed immediately if severity can not be determined. Should proceed to triage first. (H branched immediately from B on 'No', should be deferred until after triage if possible.)

[Swapped Branch Outcomes] Deploy leads to 'support resolves' check. The 'No' arrow from 'Engineering Fixes' should be to 'Notify User', not directly to 'Incident Closed'. (G loops back to D, F--"No"-->H swapped with F--"No"-->I).
[Wrong Causal Direction] Notification of resolution happens before the incident is marked as resolved. (I -> J should be J -> I)
[Illogical Loop] Marking as resolved returns to submitting a new report, starting a new incident when it should end the workflow. (J returns to A, should terminate.)
[Contradictory edge label] Resolve to be deployed to prod (D leads to G on "yes"). The 'Yes' edge from Support Resolves Incident should lead to Notification, not deployment (D--"Yes" should go to I).
[Reversed Sequence] Packaging follows Shipment Preparation (should be Packaging before Shipment Preparation).
[Swapped Branch Outcomes] Payment Successful NO leads to Cancel Order, Payment Successful YES goes to Prepare Shipment (should be logically swapped).
[Illogical Loop] Notify Customer: Out of Stock flows back to receive order (makes no sense; customer would not re-order immediately). This could be a misunderstanding but in context is not correct.
[Skipped Critical Step] No inventory replenishment is present in either branch where is out of stock (should replenish inventory or notify buyer that resupply happening).
[Wrong Merge of Parallel Paths] L (Investigate Delivery Issue) merges into K (Notify Customer: Delivered), even if not delivered.

[Wrong Causal Direction] E (Cancel Order) goes to F (Notify Customer: Out of Stock) - canceling the order should not trigger an out of stock notification, but rather a cancellation notification, especially given it could be due to payment failure. Notification of Out of Stock is the cause of potentially cancelling an order.
[Contradictory Edge Label] Delivery Successful NO goes to 'Investigate Delivery Issue', it's a 'success' edge but flows down the error path
[Reversed Sequence] Acknowledge Order after Payment Received. (Expected: Payment check then Acknowledge)
[Swapped Branch Outcomes] On ship failure, investigate, then archive. (Expected: Archive only upon successful delivery.)
[Wrong Causal Direction] Notification of Delay sends user back to Place Order *after* the delay notification. (Expected: Notifiy only if order already placed)
[Contradictory Edge Label] Prints shipping label, which leads to order cancellation (Expected: Prints shipping label then ships order)
[Illogical Loop] Send Feedback Request re-triggers re-investigation of shipping issues (Expected: Feedback should not restart logistics)
[Skipped Critical Step] No step to actually subtract inventory upon shipment.
[Wrong Merge of Parallel Paths] Cancel Order flows into Prepare Shipment (Expected: order cancel *prevents* shipment prep)
[Reversed Sequence] H[Send Order Confirmation] is shown after payment failure, should be before payment processing. `H --(No)--> I`.
[Swapped Branch Outcomes] Branch direction `B -- No --> H[Send Order Confirmation]` is incorrect for payment failure. It should trigger a payment retry or order cancellation.
[Illogical Loop] `G --> A` Order placed after update inventory.
[Reversed Sequence] `I -> J` Shipping notification is sent before invoice.
[Skipped critical step] No payment processing step exists between receiving the order and checking for payment.
[Reversed Sequence] Notification that inventory is exhausted happens *before* actually checking the inventory. (Notification of delay before decision on availability)

[Swapped Branch Outcomes] If payment is received, proceeds with the flow. If payment *isn't* received, the flow ends. But the 'No' path from 'Payment Received?' leads to Order Cancelled (as expected) but then that leads to order completion. (No-payment -> Completed makes no sense)

[Illogical Loop] When inventory is insufficient, restocking and notification happens, and then the process *re-enters inventory check*. (No clear exit after User Confirmation, should go to manual fulfillment or cancellation if user does not accept delay)

[Wrong Merge of Parallel Paths] Shipping the order leads back to "Payment Received?", an illogical step. (Should go to order processing, not back to payment). Also, shipping the user order also leads to "Order Cancelled", which makes no sense.
[Skipped Critical Step] After checking inventory, there is no step to reserve the inventory for the order, leading to potential overselling.
